newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries firm in London, gearing up for payrolls.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries firm in London, gearing up for payrolls.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries in London recovered from low Tokyo levels on Friday as the market squared up before trend-setting non-farm payroll data.
Dealers and analysts said many in the market had been taking short positions going into the 1330 GMT data, but by now the market was no longer biased one way or the other.
"I think there have been some shorts that were basically covered yesterday," said a dealer at a U.S. bank in London. "It's probably neutral."
Economists expect a relatively healthy 192,000 increase in payrolls during December after November's 118,000 rise.
The U.S. long bond at 1125 GMT was at 96-20 to yield 6.76 percent. That was up from 96-15 at the Tokyo finish but down from New York's 96-25 close.
March Treasury bond futures in automated trade were at 111-18, up from 111-13 at the Chicago close.

"The market is primed for a reasonably strong payroll number," said Brian Hilliard, senior international economist at Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull in London. "The risk for us is the hourly earnings."
Average hourly earnings are expected to show a 0.2 percent increase following a 0.8 percent rise in November.
The market's firmer tone since the Tokyo session could continue if the data fail to provide any negative shocks, analysts said.
"If it comes in as expected I think the positive tone in the market will remain in place," Hilliard said.
